history.content: What is a power of attorney job?

A power of attorney is a legal document that grants someone else the authority to act on your behalf for financial or legal matters. The signer can write a check and pay the bill for the owner and the bank must accept him/her as you.  The owner can define the scope and expiration of the power of attorney as well.  The person granted the power does not necessarily need to be a lawyer or an attorney, but could be a relative or anyone else who is trustworthy.

I'm sorry for any confusion, but your question seems to be quite broad.   A will, a living will and a durable power of attorney are all important aspects of an estate plan. In general, what happens after a person's death can depend on many factors.  If a person has a will, it will generally outline how their assets are to be distributed. If there is no will, the person is said to have died "intestate," and the distribution of assets will be determined by the laws of the jurisdiction where the person lived.
No, I meant what happens to POA upon death.

A CPA (Certified Public Accountant) with a power of attorney would charge themselves for delivering money in some cases.  The CPA, acting under the power of attorney, may be providing financial services for which they would be compensated.
what wd happen to annuity and investments?

When the owner of an annuity dies, the beneficiary might receive a single-sum distribution, which is taxed as normal income and only the amount attributable to investment income is taxed, but it will be taxed as ordinary income and not enjoy any special capital gains treatment. When there is a death benefit that exceeds the value of the account, that additional amount is also taxed as ordinary income.
Regarding investments, if the investments are held in an IRA and the owner dies, the beneficiary can either take all the money out within 5 years or choose to receive the value of the IRA at the time of the IRA owner's death in equal installments over the expected lifetime of the beneficiary. If the latter option is chosen, the IRA custodian issues the fixed-term annuity in return for the IRA assets.
